step1_figure.description: A static CMOS 3-input NAND gate consisting of three PMOS transistors in parallel and three NMOS transistors in series. The netlist ties all three inputs together to a single source (Vin), effectively operating the gate as an inverter for characterization.

switching_point_voltage.description: The input voltage (V_SP) at which the output voltage equals the input voltage (or VDD/2), representing the switching threshold of the logic gate.

equation.formula: V_SP = (sqrt(beta_n / (N^2 * beta_p)) * V_THN + (VDD - V_THP)) / (1 + sqrt(beta_n / (N^2 * beta_p)))
equation.explanation: Calculates the switching point voltage for an n-input NAND gate with all inputs tied together.
equation.assumptions: All inputs are tied together and switch simultaneously. Uses long-channel square-law MOSFET equations.

sky130_expected.reasoning: With equal W/L sizes, the series NMOS stack is weaker than the parallel PMOS network, pushing the switching point slightly above the ideal VDD/2 (0.9V).

propagation_delay_lh.description: Low-to-high propagation delay time (t_PLH) of the gate.

equation.formula: t_PLH = 0.7 * (R_p / N) * (N * C_outp + C_outn / N + C_load) ≈ 0.7 * (R_p / N) * C_load
equation.explanation: Estimates the time required for the output to transition from low to high. The simplified Eq 12.16 applies when the external load capacitance dominates.
equation.assumptions: Inputs are tied together. External load capacitance C_load is much greater than the intrinsic parasitic capacitances of the gate.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming W/L=1 and a dominant C_load = 50 fF. Equivalent PMOS resistance R_p ≈ 1 / (beta_p * (VDD - |V_THP|)) = 1 / (50e-6 * (1.8 - 0.42)) = 14.49 kOhm. t_PLH ≈ 0.7 * (14.49k / 3) * 50e-15 = 169 ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Delay is directly proportional to the load capacitance and inversely proportional to the effective width of the parallel PMOS pull-up network.

propagation_delay_hl.description: High-to-low propagation delay time (t_PHL) of the gate.

equation.formula: t_PHL = 0.7 * N * R_n * (N * C_outp + C_outn / N + C_load) + 0.35 * R_n * C_oxn * N^2 ≈ 0.7 * N * R_n * C_load
equation.explanation: Estimates the time required for the output to transition from high to low through the series NMOS stack. Eq 12.18 is the simplified form for a dominant load.
equation.assumptions: Inputs are tied together. External load capacitance C_load is much greater than the intrinsic parasitic capacitances.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming W/L=1 and a dominant C_load = 50 fF. Equivalent NMOS resistance R_n ≈ 1 / (beta_n * (VDD - V_THN)) = 1 / (270e-6 * (1.8 - 0.42)) = 2.68 kOhm. t_PHL ≈ 0.7 * 3 * 2.68k * 50e-15 = 281 ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The series connection of N NMOS transistors multiplies the effective pull-down resistance by N, making the high-to-low transition slower than a simple inverter of the same size.

step3_testbench.description: Measures the switching point voltage (V_SP) via DC sweep and the propagation delays (t_PLH, t_PHL) via Transient analysis for a 3-input NAND gate driving a 50fF load.
step3_testbench.spice:
* 3-input NAND gate characterization testbench
.lib ${SKY130_PDK} tt

* Define parameterized widths and lengths (assuming minimum size for baseline)
.param W_xm1=1u L_xm1=0.15u
.param W_xm2=1u L_xm2=0.15u
.param W_xm3=1u L_xm3=0.15u
.param W_xm4=1u L_xm4=0.15u
.param W_xm5=1u L_xm5=0.15u
.param W_xm6=1u L_xm6=0.15u

* --- DUT (Device Under Test) ---
xm2 P001 Vin P002 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm2} l={L_xm2}
Vin Vin 0 0
VDD VDD 0 1.8
xm4 Vout Vin VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm4} l={L_xm4}
xm5 Vout Vin VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm5} l={L_xm5}
xm3 Vout Vin P001 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm3} l={L_xm3}
xm1 P002 Vin 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1} l={L_xm1}
xm6 Vout Vin VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm6} l={L_xm6}

* --- Load Capacitance ---
Cload Vout 0 50f

.control
* 1. DC Analysis for Switching Point Voltage (V_SP)
dc Vin 0 1.8 0.01
meas dc vsp when v(Vout)=0.9
print vsp

* 2. Transient Analysis for Propagation Delays (t_PLH, t_PHL)
* Alter the Vin source to act as a pulse generator for the transient run
alter @Vin[pulse] = [ 0 1.8 1n 0.05n 0.05n 2n 4n ]
tran 10p 6n

* Measure delays at 50% of VDD (0.9V)
meas tran tplh trig v(Vin) val=0.9 fall=1 targ v(Vout) val=0.9 rise=1
meas tran tphl trig v(Vin) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(Vout) val=0.9 fall=1
print tplh tphl

quit
.endc
.end
